text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorkInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
FromCSDept(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakingDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x is taking the database course.
TakingClassWithProfessorD(x) ::: x is taking a class with Professor David.
WorkInLab(x) ::: x is working in the lab.
James ::: James is a specific individual.
Question: James is a student working in the lab and does not work in the lab or have a part-time job offered by the university.

Premises:
¬(WorkInLab(James) ∧ PartTimeJob(James)) ::: James doesn't work in the lab or have a part-time job offered by the university.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ WorkInLab(x)) → ¬PartTimeJob(x)) ::: None of the students who work in the library have part-time jobs offered by the university.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x)) → WorkInLibrary(x)) ::: All students with part-time jobs offered by the university work in the library.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ TakingDatabaseCourse(x)) → FromCSDept(x)) ::: All students taking the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ TakingClassWithProfessorD(x)) → TakingDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All students taking a class with Professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorkInLab(x) → TakingClassWithProfessorD(x)) ::: All students working in the lab are taking a class with Professor David.

Conclusion:
TakingDatabaseCourse(James) ::: James takes the database course.
